role.altitude: The reporter keeps judging what matters, checking with sources, choosing the angle and deciding the shape of the story; typing out recordings, hunting through mails for tips and searching the archive by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking every machine-found quote and fact against the recording or source
role.ambitious_version: A reporter who leaves an interview with a checked quote list and spends the saved hour on one more call.

tasks.short: Have recorded interviews transcribed, review and evaluate notes taken about news events to isolate pertinent facts, quotes and details, check quotes against the recording, mark what needs confirming and build the fact list for the story.

steps.what: Reporter types out the recorded interview from the audio
Reporter reads the listed candidate facts and quotes with speaker and time code

loop.input: The machine transcript of an on-record interview and the reporter's story question.
loop.output: A list of candidate facts and quotes, each with the speaker and the time code in the recording.
loop.check: Every quote must appear word for word in the transcript at the given time code, or it is dropped; the reporter decides what is pertinent and marks it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A search finds words the reporter already knows; it cannot list what a long interview said.

steps.what: Reporter evaluates the notes and transcripts to isolate the pertinent facts, quotes and details
Reporter checks each quote to be used against the recording
Reporter weighs conflicting accounts and marks the facts that need confirmation from a second source
Reporter writes the fact list with sources for the story

tasks.design: The reporter uploads on-record interview recordings to the transcription service the publisher has a processing contract with, which returns a Dutch machine transcript with time codes; the reporter corrects names and unclear passages. A bounded step lists candidate facts and quotes from the transcript, each with speaker and time code, and drops any quote not found word for word. Clicking a time code plays that spot, so checking a quote takes seconds. Judging what matters, weighing conflicting accounts and the fact list stay with the reporter. Recordings with confidential sources are never uploaded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Long recordings had to be typed out before anything could be found in them.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch machine transcription with time codes, and models that list quotes that can be checked word for word.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing which detail is the story.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a source avoided saying.
tasks.altitude: Less typing after interviews; editorial judgement does not change.

reach.learn: Whether time-coded quotes cut questions back to the reporter.

evidence.claim: A Dutch service sells machine transcripts ("90%+ accurate") and human-checked ones ("99%+").
A former editor-in-chief was suspended for AI-invented quotes, so every quote must be found word for word in the recording.
The Dutch journalists' union model guideline says no confidential or personal data go into AI tools and asks for a final check by another person.

assumptions: Boundary: from notes and recordings to the fact list; writing the story is a separate task.

Input contract for s1: recordings made by the reporter on phone or recorder and uploaded to the contracted transcription service, which returns a transcript with time codes; fallback is typing out by hand.
Coverage: about 80% of recorded interviews are on the record and may be uploaded; confidential-source recordings are typed by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: the machine transcript from s1; handwritten scene notes are read as today.
The newsroom's AI policy allows the contracted service for on-record material.
unknowns: Hours of recorded interview per reporter per week.
research_questions: How many machine-listed quotes are wrong or cut short?

already_counted.description: Reporter corrects names and unclear passages in the machine transcript.
Reporter reads the listed quotes against the transcript before marking them.

incremental.description: Reporter uploads recordings and labels them on-record or confidential.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly handwritten notes at the scene and short calls; high: long recorded on-record interviews for background pieces.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive assignments from the desk, collect reader tips, evaluate leads or tips, check what was published before, check with the tipster or a source and develop the story idea for the desk.

steps.what: Desk editor gives the reporter assignments in the morning meeting or by chat
Readers send tips by mail, WhatsApp or the tip form on the site
Reporter reads assignments, leads and tips spread over the tip mailbox, WhatsApp and chat
Reporter searches the archive to see what was published before on the lead

loop.input: The names, place and subject from the lead, and the outlet's own archive of published stories.
loop.output: A few lines on what the outlet already published, each with the date and a link to the article.
loop.check: Every line must link to an archive article that opens and contains the name or subject, or it is dropped; the reporter opens the articles that matter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Archive search returns many hits; the reporter needs to know quickly whether the angle is new.

steps.what: Reporter calls the tipster or a source to check whether the lead holds
Reporter evaluates the lead and develops the story idea for the desk

tasks.design: Tips from the site form, the tip mailbox and the WhatsApp tip line land in one tip list in the newsroom planning tool, with where, when and contact as fields and repeats of the same tip grouped, so the reporter reads one list. For a lead, a bounded step summarises what the outlet already published from its own archive, with a link per article. Checking with the tipster and developing the idea stay with the reporter; no tool ranks tips for newsworthiness.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tips were spread over mailboxes and phones, and the archive had to be searched hit by hit.
tasks.enabler_now: Newsrooms test archive chatbots; tip forms and shared inboxes are standard configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a real tip from a grudge.
tasks.human_edge: Sources who call this reporter because they trust them.
tasks.altitude: Less searching; choosing stories stays with reporter and desk.

reach.learn: Whether one tip list shows which tips no one followed up.

evidence.claim: A Dutch newspaper tests an archive chatbot for reader questions.
In a broadcaster study, 45% of AI-assistant news answers had a significant issue, so every summary line must link to an article.
Purely journalistic processing of tipsters' data is largely exempt from GDPR duties under the Dutch implementation act.

assumptions: Boundary: from assignments and tips to the story idea; pitching in the meeting is covered in another task.

Input contract for s3: tips entered by readers on the site form with about the effort of an e-mail (s2), plus the tip mailbox and WhatsApp line routed into the planning tool by the newsroom's IT; assignments posted by the desk editor in s1.
Input contract for s4: the outlet's own published stories in the CMS archive, indexed for the summary; older paper cuttings are not covered, about 80% of archive questions are answered from it.
Calls and evaluation keep their full time; desk editor and reader time are outside the reporter's savings.
unknowns: Tips per day and how many are repeats.
research_questions: Does a single tip list change which tips are followed up?

already_counted.description: Reporter opens archive articles behind summary lines that matter.

incremental.description: Reporter marks handled tips in the tip list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a reporter working mostly from desk assignments; high: a regional reporter who handles many reader tips.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check reference materials, such as the archive and news files, public records and reports, to obtain relevant facts, note each fact with its source and check conflicting facts.

steps.what: Reporter searches the archive and news files for background on people, places and earlier events

loop.input: The reporter's background question and the outlet's archive of published stories and agency copy.
loop.output: A short answer with the facts found, each tied to a dated archive article.
loop.check: Every fact must quote an archive article that opens, or it is dropped; facts older than the latest correction are flagged; the reporter reads the cited articles before using a fact.
loop.stop: One answer per question; a question with no cited facts returns nothing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search returns hundreds of hits for a common name.

steps.what: Reporter looks up public records such as the trade register, land registry, court rulings and council papers
Reporter reads reference books, reports and statistics for relevant facts

loop.input: A long public report or policy paper the reporter selects.
loop.check: Every finding must quote the page it cites, or it is dropped; the reporter reads the pages used in the story.
loop.why_not_simpler: The table of contents does not show which findings bear on the story.

steps.what: Reporter notes each fact with its source in the story notes
Reporter checks conflicting facts with a second source

tasks.design: An answer desk over the outlet's own archive and agency copy answers background questions with each fact tied to a dated article, and a bounded step summarises long public reports with page numbers. Both carry their links into the story notes, so the reporter copies less. Public records such as the trade register and court rulings are still looked up by the reporter at the source, and conflicting facts are checked with a second source.
tasks.previous_blocker: The archive answered only keyword searches, and long reports had to be read end to end.
tasks.enabler_now: Archive chatbots in newsrooms and models that summarise with page references.
tasks.still_hard: Facts that are only in a register or a person's memory.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a fact repeated for years was never true.
tasks.altitude: Less searching; the reporter still owns every fact.

reach.task: Keep the archive indexed and corrected
reach.learn: Which archive questions the answer desk cannot answer.

evidence.claim: A Dutch newspaper tests an archive chatbot, and over 30 Dutch news brands opened their archives to a Dutch language model.
In a broadcaster study, 45% of AI-assistant news answers had a significant issue, so every fact must cite an article.
Text and data mining of protected works is allowed unless the maker opted out machine-readably.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reporter's question to confirmed facts; writing is a separate task.

Input contract for s1: the outlet's published stories and agency copy in the CMS archive, indexed by the archive team; about 80% of background questions are about the digital years; older paper cuttings are searched as today; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: reports the reporter selects as files or links; reports behind paywalls are read as today.
Public record lookups and second-source checks keep most or all of their time.
unknowns: How far back the digital archive goes.
research_questions: How often does the answer desk cite an article that does not support the fact?

already_counted.description: Reporter reads cited archive articles before using a fact.
Reporter reads the cited report pages.

incremental.description: Reporter reports wrong answers to the archive team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stories built on public records and calls; high: background pieces with long archive histories and reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree the slot with the desk, determine a published or broadcast story's emphasis, length and format, organize the material into an outline, fit the length, draft versions for web, radio and push, and have the desk check the final story and versions.

steps.what: Reporter agrees length, format and slot with the desk editor
Reporter determines the story's emphasis and opening
Reporter organizes notes and material into an outline in the chosen order

loop.input: The reporter's chosen emphasis, the slot length and the fact list with sources.
loop.output: A draft outline: the order of points, each tied to an item on the fact list.
loop.check: Every point must refer to a fact-list item, or it is dropped; no new facts are added; the reporter reorders and edits.
loop.stop: One outline per emphasis; a new emphasis starts a new draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives sections; ordering many facts for this emphasis needs reading them.

steps.what: Reporter fits the text to the agreed length or air time
Reporter rewrites the story in other formats: a short web version, a radio script and a push alert

loop.input: The final main story as filed to the desk, and the length rules per format.
loop.output: Draft versions for web, radio and push, within the length rule of each format.
loop.check: Every fact, name and number in a version must appear in the main story, or the sentence is marked; quotes are kept verbatim; the reporter edits every version.
loop.stop: One draft per format per filed version of the main story.
loop.why_not_simpler: Cutting to length drops sentences; a radio script needs spoken sentences.

steps.what: Desk editor checks the final story and its versions under editorial responsibility

tasks.design: Deciding the emphasis and agreeing the slot stay with reporter and desk. In the CMS ({OTHER}) a length counter shows the room left in the slot, and a bounded step drafts an outline from the reporter's fact list for the chosen emphasis, adding no new facts. From the filed main story, the same kind of step drafts the web, radio and push versions, checked against the main story; the reporter edits each and the desk editor checks story and versions before publication, so they fall under editorial responsibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each format was rewritten from scratch by the reporter or a channel editor.
tasks.enabler_now: Models draft radio scripts from articles; a Dutch news agency tests this with a university.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what the story is really about.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the audience of each channel needs to hear first.

ambition.what: Radio listeners and push readers reached with stories that today only appear in print or online.

tasks.altitude: Less rewriting per format; the emphasis and final check stay with people.

reach.learn: Whether drafted radio versions need less rewriting than print copy.

evidence.claim: A Dutch news agency and a university test turning articles into radio scripts with language models.
AI-made text on matters of public interest needs a label unless a person reviews it under editorial responsibility.
The journalists' union guideline asks for a final check by another person.

assumptions: Boundary: from the agreed slot to the story and versions checked by the desk; publishing is the desk's work.
Input contract for s3: the fact list the reporter writes in the notes task; fallback is outlining from notes.
Input contract for s5: the main story as filed in the CMS; about half of stories get extra format versions.
Agreeing the slot and the emphasis keep their full time; the desk editor's check is outside the reporter's savings.
unknowns: How many stories get radio or push versions today.
research_questions: Do drafted versions add errors the desk must catch?

already_counted.description: Reporter edits drafted format versions and fixes marked sentences.

incremental.description: Reporter keeps the length rules per format current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: print-only stories with a set length; high: stories that go to web, radio and push.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
